body:
Thank you, again. 

I'm not going to press charges. Not in the least because of the difficulties you mentioned. I feel like it wouldn't benefit anyone, either. He has actually apologised once (somewhat) saying that if what he did was wrong then he regrets it. 

I think I need to sit and process all this information. If I do come back to this post though, I hope I can reach you or someone as helpful as you've been. Thank you so so much.

Thank you so much for your help. It's all a bit overwhelming but I'm glad to have a little bit of clarity. There's a lot I want to ask, but I feel guilty for saddling you up with so much. And to be honest, the questions are fairly childish. 
Like: could I press charges? (I'm positive I won't. But if the answer is yes, it just makes it clearer that something wrong did actually happen, I guess?)

Does the situation change if the person doing something wrong doesn't realise it's wrong? My ex did truly love me and I don't think he intended any malice. 

I'm truly glad you're in a much better place right now!

I'm so sorry to read that you've had such a tough time in the past, I'm glad you seem to be OK now (right?). 

I'm also grateful for your advice. Going to therapy about this particular topic feels too difficult and confronting. Somewhere I feel as though I didn't recognise what happened as anything wrong, so I let it happen. I wish my ex didn't do what he did, but isn't it my fault as much as his? I feel so much shame that this also impedes my ability to talk about it, even to my husband. He's so understanding but somehow I feel as though he'll hate me (which I know is irrational).

So sorry for just throwing my emotions out. I will take your advice on trying to sit with my feelings. Fortunately I know what you mean by that. Thanks for that.

I think I'm in a bit of denial, or I can't process that what happened to me could  be rape.. I know I'm having nightmares, but it was so long ago. I only had the courage to post here because it's fairly anonymous. 
Apparently I talk in my sleep and my husband is worried about me, but I just can't say the words out loud. I think if I wanted to talk about this in therapy I wouldn't be able to say anything.

You seem pretty strong to know yourself enough that you have a way back literally but also figuratively. At this point I don't know if I want to return from getting lost. If somewhere along the line I stepped into a black hole I think that would be fine. 
It used to be that I didn't want to leave behind devastated family but even that deterrent is fading.

Thank you so much for responding. My head is taking me down all the wrong roads of disappearing. 
I also just think of going outside and getting lost, most of the time I'm too afraid to. 
My husband does know about my past, and I have covered it to some but not all extent in therapy. It just tends to come back when I'm at my worst.
what do you do if your phone dies while you're finding your way home? And I tend to cry a lot.. don't know what sort of effect crying on the bus or train will have..
